items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Story 1 gives payment by butterfat test rather than milk weight, but never says the test of the station where he delivers governs (second bolded element).
Story 1: without payment-by-test a low reading 'would have cost nobody anything'.
Loomis secretary from 1901 (Story 1), bookkeeper Teague (Story 6), buttermaker Hobart Sill at Larrow Green (Story 2).
Section A calls Selby Vose manager but never says he was Gideon's son and never gives the 1913 start. Those appear only in B3, and E16 leaves 1911 vs 1913 unresolved.

Story 6 describes the station-gain line and the 5 1/4 percent figure but says Teague 'invented' it in 1905. The key scores this item on the line's 1898 origin (scope rule); r05's 1905 self-refutation was adopted.
Story 2: Ostrey Hollow station seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Section A never describes weighing, composite sampling, the percent read on the bottle neck or the fixed pipette charge.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897 (the 1898 dating is rejected).
Story 2: 6 doz pipettes at 17.6 c.c., itemized invoice totaling $77.93.
Story 3: gap of 0.19 'constant in every season', which rules out a seasonal cause.
Section A never says the pipette could not be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Keddie was tester from the station's opening on 4 May 1896 (Story 2) and was dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 5).
Nothing on the test book's columns or on keeping it in one hand with initialed corrections.
Both figures are in Section A: 3.61 recorded (Story 3) and 3.80 in 1896 before the faulty glass (Story 8).
Story 4: broke 8 May, borrowed until 10 July, nine weeks, tests rose then fell back, question mark. The 3.80 figure is absent, but the core fact (no REQUIRED line) is present.
Story 6: Emmet Brant, largest patron, was Keddie's brother-in-law through his sister Orra.
The 1919 circular is present, but the content of Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as taught, cannot say why') is not.
Story 5: died 1934 without public vindication.
Six farms of Hessel Bottom (Story 2); Brant the largest (Story 6).
Story 6: Brant's weigh book from 1897; his scale and the station's consistently agreed.

Story 3 sets 3.61 against Larrow Green's 3.78 and then gives the chronic gap as 'nineteen hundredths'. C1b rejects r09's 0.17. This merges the visible 0.17 gap with the true 0.19 shortfall, which loses the item by rule.
Story 3: Grigg committee of 1908 advanced wet hay and sampled only January-March. Reported as the committee's theory, not as fact.
200,000 lb at 3.42 is in Story 6, but Section A never says the loss was proportional (richer herds lost more).
Custody is only cited ('r18 full custody chain'); Roy Brant, 1929 and the 1958 loan to Ivy are not stated.
No Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd as founder in Section A.
Story 8: four Hessel Bottom farmers' milk delivered elsewhere across sixteen summers. The 1915 start is absent, but the core fact is present.
Only 'independent Alder Corners test records' (the artifact, one element). No other county, other glassware or uncompared book; at least two elements are required.
Story 8: the same four men's milk tested 3.78-3.82 across sixteen summers against the station's 3.61, roughly 0.19 higher.
Says only that 'land and cattle were never at fault'. Does not say that the same milk tested differently in two buildings, killing the hay and watering explanations together.
Story 8: Rosalie Cudd, daughter not niece, supplied sixteen summers of figures to Ivy.
Story 7 has Strawn checking with the lactometer 'every year since 1908'. That is NT-23's 1908 against the bolded 1907-1936.
Section A says he ran the lactometer but never that he found no added water. That appears only in F.
Story 7: 12 June 1923, pipettes run against a burette, whole crate condemned.
Nothing on Strawn writing no figure for the deficiency or making no further report.
Replacement ordered 'same week', in use within the month, but no 28 June / 2 July order dates and no 1924 average of 3.80 anywhere in Section A.
Crate to the loft is present; the notebooks' 1947 move to the college library is absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Story 5: petitioned January 1925.
Story 5: Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, two of three sittings at the station.
Story 3: watering (Vose), theft via Teague's testimony and wet hay were all argued; Story 5: 'no cause established'.
The four books are listed, but nothing says the 1923 notebook contained the answer and was read for its other lines.
Story 5: dismissed 30 April 1925 before the award, no cause found; $3,800 without admission, charged to the station account.
Section A never states the one-fifth fraction or that the award was charged to the account where the loss had accrued as 'gain'.
Story 8: granddaughter, graduate student at State Agricultural College at Farland, with Prof. Leland Vaught.
Only the Alder Corners cross-check is mentioned. She is not described as assembling the scattered record series.
Story 8: February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine pipettes.
Story 8: 9 March 1958, 16.72 c.c. vs 17.6, 95 percent of the mark.
95 percent (Story 8), true 3.80 (Story 8) against recorded 3.61 with 0.19 short (Story 3).
76,000 lb and $19,000 are in Story 8, but the 40,000,000 lb milk figure and the ledger identity are absent from Section A. REQUIRED needs all four.
Bulletin 471 of October 1958 is present; the 35/33/24-year intervals (second bolded element) are not.
Granddaughter.
Derived via Duncan, citing r18 and r22's correction.
Second cousins via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
A08: leaves full vs half sibling open and says it does not change the answer.
Gideon Vose, son not nephew.
Gideon wrote Article VII; the son later blamed the patrons for the stakes that rule created.
A01 asserted: 'None... Resolved in favor of no relationship.'
The key gives 0 on both points when the answer asserts a verdict; the answer treats the family denial as settling the question.
True test 3.60; 360 lb owed.
Gives $90.00 at $0.25 without saying it is using the period average instead of the 1910 price of 24 cents. The key wants $86.40.
76,000 lb; 5.26 percent of credited and 5.00 percent of delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 with the sum shown.
72 pipettes, each 0.88 c.c. short.
Gives only 'about 26 years', not the exact 26 years and 6 weeks (or equivalent) the key requires.
A02 asserted: 'about nine hundred thousand pounds' preferred over r23.
Variable: the pipette/measuring glass.
Same tester, same herds/patrons, same season.
Says tests 'rose' and 'fell back to the prior level' without the bolded 3.80 and 3.61.
Isolates the glass and rules out herds, season and tester honesty. Limit: does not identify the specific fault; that needed the 1958 measurement.
Only two distinct reasons: the 1911 interval and the cream arriving heavy. Sill's 'weighed in heavy' is the same fact as the ledger surplus, not a third reason.
Calls the ledger surplus and Sill's heavy-cream observation independent, but both rest on the same event (the station cream arriving heavy at Larrow Green).
A09 asserted: 'Only once: Teague raised the persistent gain with manager Vose in 1916'.
Yes as to effect; cites the 1902 grievance and the 1919 circular.

Only two of the five in B-G: signed the gain-line sheets and wrote the 1919 circular. Manager from 1913 is left unresolved (E16). The hearing argument and the no-glassware-in-his-hand point are absent.
A03 asserted. The headline verdict 'no, as to the cause' has no declining qualifier; the answer also says the gain line and Teague's warning showed him his explanation could not be right.
Crate location resolved to the loft by the finder's account and witnesses (E6); Rosalie daughter vs niece by her own letter and r18 (E15); great-niece vs granddaughter by family record (E13/B1).
Pairs named with breakers: NT-16 eleven pipettes (r12/r19) broken by the measurement sheet; NT-9 $3,500 (r01/r21) by the minute book; NT-14 $77.39 (r19/r20) by r20's own table. Also NT-2 and NT-11.
A10 (Article VII year): says it cannot be determined because the minute book was lost. A04 is not declined (leans toward the reground-mold accident) and A06 is not addressed.
r15's 'whole of 1908' against its own report (E19); r20's $77.39 against its own table (E10).
1897 crate of pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95 percent, proportional not a fixed offset. Onset from the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80; ends at the 1923 condemnation; nothing on the farms changed.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer record.
Theft (Teague) defeated by the station-gain surplus and the 1911 interval.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter against a constant 0.19 gap.
A07 asserted: 'No.'
A05 asserted: 'He privately suspected the glass as early as summer 1911' and later blamed the patrons; stated as fact, not declined.
The summary is 151 words (hyphenated compounds counted as one, dashes not counted), over the 150 limit, although the heading says <=150.
Only the ledgers and the 1958 measurement are named; at least five are required.
No decoy adopted and no wrong headline figure.
5 percent short, 1897, $19,000, 1958, Ansel named. Covers both ends.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Strawn's circuit dated from 1908 (NT-23), asserted in Story 7 ('every year since 1908') and F ('every visit from 1908 on')
Gullibility A02: 1896 intake asserted as about 900,000 lb (C5b, Story 2)
Gullibility A03: 'no, as to the cause' verdict on whether Vose knew the tests were understated (D3)
Gullibility A05: tester's belief asserted, suspected the glass in 1911 and blamed the patrons in 1925 (F, Stories 4-5)
Gullibility A07: 'No' on whether the board examined the glassware (F)
Gullibility A09: Teague asserted to have questioned the gain with Vose in 1916 (D2, Story 6)
